title: Brenner's Verity Notebook
description: The web archive of Hal Brenner's monthly county letter out of Gridfall: one sourced piece a month, each one ending in the documents it came out of.

data.author: Hal Brenner
data.tagline: County government, one piece a month. Gridfall, Verity County.
data.about:
Hal Brenner. Gridfall. County reporter at the Gridfall Ledger from 1999 to October 2019.

One piece a month, the third Tuesday. $5 a month, 312 subscribers. Terms are on the [url=/post/subscribe]subscribe page[/url].

This site is the archive and it is free. The letter is sent by a list service at [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]brenners-notebook.email[/url], which keeps its own copies back to issue 69. The list moved there in December 2025, so everything before issue 69 is here and nowhere else.

In the letter and not here: the short items, the diary of what meets when, and the paid notice when there is one.

Comments are off and have been since 2020. What sits under a piece is reader mail, printed with the writer's leave and typed in by me. The form at the bottom of each entry has not worked in years.

Every document named at the end of a piece, I have. Say which one and I will send it scanned, the same day, for nothing.

blogroll.label: Verity Valley Water Board - minutes, rates, notices

posts.title: Subscribe
posts.body:
$5 a month. 312 people pay it.

One piece a month, sent on the third Tuesday. The piece is the whole of it; there is no second tier and no annual rate and there is not going to be one.

The archive on this site is free and always has been. Everything a subscriber gets on the Tuesday is here by the evening.

To start, pay by card through the list service at [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]brenners-notebook.email[/url], or post me a cheque and I will put you on for the year.

To stop, the link at the bottom of any issue works on the first click and does not ask you anything.

If you want it and $5 a month is not on, write and say so. There is no form for that.

The list is not sold or rented, and there is no advertising on this site.

posts.title: Line 4410-52
posts.body:
The county is required to publish its legal notices in a newspaper. State statute 18-2201, passed in 1953 and amended in 1978 and 1994, neither time on this clause, says notice of a public hearing, a tax sale, a bond authorisation or a zoning amendment shall run in a newspaper of general circulation published within the county.

One outlet meets that description. The Gridfall Ledger, which is now [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url], owned by Pinelock Media Group, with no reporter in this county since 2019 and nobody filing copy since 2023.

Line 4410-52 of the county budget is legal notices. It was $19,400 in the year to June. The 2027 draft carries $21,100. The rate is $14.60 per column inch. It is set by the vendor and accepted by the county and it has never been bid, because a bid needs two bidders.

The notice of the 13 October capital vote ran on 2 September. The text of it is correct to the comma. It was typed by a clerk in the county building and sent over as a block the vendor is contractually forbidden to edit, which is why it is the only thing on that site this month written by a person, and the person works for the county.

Around it, under an auto-generated headline, are three paragraphs nobody typed. One of them gives the county's population as 41,000. It has been about 28,400 since the last count and it has never been 41,000.

The statute requires the notice. It does not require anything printed around the notice to be true, and in 1953 there was no reason to think about that.

I put three questions to Pinelock in writing on 7 September. Whether any employee of the group resides in Verity County. Whether any part of the production of the legal notice contract is performed by a person. Whether $14.60 is the rate charged to the other nine counties in the group. The reply, on 11 September, is six sentences about serving the communities it serves and one about not disclosing commercial terms, and it is the answer to all three.

It also calls the Ledger a trusted local source since 1889. The paper was founded in 1891 and says so on the masthead of every issue in the [url=synth://verityledger.com/]archive Pinelock still hosts[/url]. 1889 is Halloran Communications, which bought it in 2011. I have sent the correction to the address on [url=synth://pinelock-media.com/]the company site[/url], which has said Careers: coming soon since 2019.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]2027 budget draft, page 112, line 4410-52, with the prior year actual in the second column. The draft is 214 pages and pages 140 to 214 are a scan with no text layer.[*]State statute 18-2201, one paragraph, and the 1978 and 1994 session laws amending it.[*]Affidavit of publication for the notice of 2 September 2026, one page, from the clerk of the board.[*]Pinelock Media Group, letter of 11 September 2026, one page.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-77]issue 77[/url].

comments.author: Charlene Rupp, clerk, Verity Valley Water Board
comments.body: $14.60 an inch is what we paid too. Our hearing notice last October was 14.5 inches and came to $211.70, and the table in it was printed with the base charge under the heading for gallons. The affidavit came back signed and I filed it without reading the printed version, which is on me and not on them.

posts.title: Six lots and no letter
posts.body:
A man on Kestrel Road rang me on 3 August to ask who he complains to about a road being cut in behind his property. I told him the planning commission, that there would have been a hearing, and that he would have had a letter. He said he had not. I checked on the assumption that he had thrown it out, because most people have.

There was no letter. There has not been a letter to anybody in this county since 2021.

Zoning Ordinance section 7-114, as it stood from 1994 to 2021: written notice by first class mail to the owners of record of all abutting parcels, not less than ten days before the hearing.

Section 7-114 as amended on 14 September 2021: notice shall be posted to the county's official website for a period of not less than ten days.

The amendment was one of fourteen housekeeping changes recommended by outside counsel to bring the ordinance into line with state law. State law does permit website notice. State law does not require anybody to stop mailing. Nothing in the packet says the county intends to stop mailing and the minutes record no discussion of it. Mailing stopped because the clerk's office read the ordinance and did what it says.

The posting is a PDF uploaded to a directory. There is no page that lists the directory. It is not on the services index, it is not on the planning page, and the portal's own search does not return it, because the search indexes pages and this is a file. I found the Kestrel Road one by asking the clerk for the file name and then asking the site for the file name.

Six lots, north side of Kestrel Road, between the old crossing and the Ashkettle line. Approved on consent on 7 July, no discussion, no objectors. There were no objectors because nobody knew.

The county's own estimate, which I asked for and had in two days, which I want to note because it does not usually go like that: about forty abutting-owner letters a year at roughly $0.73 each with the envelope and the clerk's time. Thirty dollars a year, and an afternoon to amend the ordinance.

I have put that to three of the five board members. Two said it sounded reasonable. One asked whether anybody had complained, which is the question that sends this round again, because the people who would complain are the people who were not told.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Zoning Ordinance section 7-114, current text and the 1994 text. Two pages together.[*]Board packet of 14 September 2021, item 9, the fourteen housekeeping amendments, and the minutes of that meeting, which are four pages.[*]Planning commission minutes, 7 July 2026, item 4, the Kestrel Road minor subdivision, approved on consent.[*]Administrative Services estimate of the cost of mailed notice, 11 August 2026, half a page in an email.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-76]issue 76[/url].

comments.author: the man on Kestrel Road
comments.body: For the record I am not against the lots. I would have gone to the hearing and said my piece about the culvert and then gone home. That is all I wanted and that is the part I did not get.

posts.title: Nineteen parcels and a mailbox
posts.body:
The county tax sale was on 16 June, in the basement of the county building, eleven people in the room and two on the phone. Sixty-one parcels offered, fifty-four sold, seven struck to the county because nobody bid the minimum.

Nineteen of the fifty-four went to one buyer, Corbin Hollow Holdings LLC, for $41,380. Six in Coyne Flats, five in Halsey, four in New Carrow, three in Gridfall, one out past Ashkettle. Average price $2,178. Three are buildable lots, two have houses standing on them, and the rest are strips, halves of strips, and a triangle behind a church that cannot be reached from a road.

The deeds are recorded and are in the [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/land-records]land records index[/url] under that name. The registered agent's address is a suite number in another state which I make the registered address of a little over nine hundred companies. The company's own page, at [url=synth://corbinhollowholdings.biz]corbinhollowholdings.biz[/url], is a photograph of a skyline that is not in this state and a contact form that returns an error. I have written to the agent twice. An agent is not required to pass anything on and this one has not.

The strategy is to hold them and do nothing, and it works. Nobody is going to develop a triangle behind a church. The tax on the nineteen runs to a few hundred dollars a year in total. If it is not paid the parcels come back to the sale in three years and can be bought again, by anybody, including by the same buyer.

If the grass is four feet high, nuisance abatement runs about fourteen months from complaint to mowing, costs the county roughly $340 a parcel, and ends in a lien against a company with no assets in this state. The lien sits on a parcel worth less than the lien, and that is the end of the process. There is no next step.

Nothing unlawful has happened at any point above.

Three counties within an hour of here have fixed it, and the fix is four sentences: a bidder registration rule requiring a name, a street address, a certificate of good standing and no delinquent tax owed anywhere in the county. It goes in the sale resolution, which the board passes fresh every year, so it does not need an ordinance amendment.

I put that to the treasurer on 9 July. She said, on the record, that she had raised it in 2024 and been told it would reduce the number of bidders. It would. That is what it is for.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Tax sale list as published under section 24-19, thirty days before the sale. Four pages of small type.[*]The nineteen deeds by instrument number, recorded 24 and 25 June 2026. Viewing the images is free; certified copies are $4 a page and you do not need certified copies.[*]Sale resolution 2026-2, adopted in March, two pages. The registration rule would go at paragraph 6.[*]Corbin Hollow Holdings LLC, registration and agent filing from the state register, two pages.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-75]issue 75[/url].

comments.author: a bidder who was in the room
comments.body: Two of us stopped bidding on the Halsey ones by about the sixth. Not because we were run up. Once you know it is one buyer who is not going to stop, you are only paying more for the one you get.

posts.title: The fire, once
posts.body:
Thursday was twenty-three years. I have not written about the substation fire since 2019 and did not intend to again. I am doing it once, in one place, and then going back to the budget.

The reason is not the anniversary. In April I went through forty of the retellings that are now the first thing anybody finds. Thirty-one of the forty give the year as 1994 or 2004. Twenty-six say lightning. Nine say two people died.

[b]4:52 a.m., Wednesday 11 June 2003.[/b] Substation No. 3, the fenced transformer yard at Depot and Quarry Road, Gridfall. That time is from the Gridfall fire department's run sheet, which is a public document and which I have had since the 13th of that month.

It burned about six hours. Roughly 4,100 Verity Valley customers lost power. Most were back inside two days. Some were out five.

[b]Nobody died.[/b] Two Gridfall volunteer firefighters were treated for smoke inhalation at County General in Marchfield and released the same afternoon. I spoke to both of them that week.

The state utility commission's summary is dated November 2003 and is two pages. The cause given is insulation degradation consistent with age. That is the whole finding. Verity Valley Power and Light ran its own internal investigation and has never released it. I asked in 2003, in 2009, and again on 2 March this year. Three refusals, all courteous, all the same refusal.

There was no lightning. There was no thunderstorm over this county that night and the county airport's hourly observations say so. The lightning is in the retellings because a substation fire is a thing people already have a picture of, and the picture has lightning in it.

The Ledger's own 2026 site runs the wrong year and the lightning, because the pipeline scraped it off the farms and the farms scraped it off each other.

One thing of mine. My piece of 12 June 2003 used the word explosion. It was a headline word and I let it into the copy. A transformer failed and burned. There was a loud failure at the start which people three streets away heard and described to me as an explosion, and I took their word, which is what you do, and then printed it as mine, which is not. Walt Pennock wrote to the paper about it that July. He was right, he was polite about it, and we ran three lines at the bottom of page four, which is not a correction, it is a way of having technically done one.

I am setting that out because explosion is in about a dozen of the forty, and at least two of them are, at some remove, quoting me.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Gridfall fire department run sheet, 11 June 2003, two pages. Times of call, arrival, water on and release.[*]State utility commission, summary of investigation, November 2003, two pages. The records office emails it, no fee.[*]County airport hourly observations, 10 and 11 June 2003, four pages.[*]The Gridfall Ledger for 12 June 2003, page one. Microfilm at Marchfield; it is past where the scanning stops.[*]The wiki article at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]wiki.gridfall.net[/url], which has the date right and is better sourced than anything published about it this year.[/list]

Write and I will send you the first two, scanned, today, for nothing. I would rather you had them than took my word for it.

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-74]issue 74[/url].

comments.author: Walt Pennock
comments.body:
Two things on the times, neither of which changes what you wrote.

4:52 is when the call came in to the hall. It is not when the bank failed. The yard was dark before that and the tie from Pell picked up what it could at about 4:49 by the recorder, which is a machine and does not round.

4,100 is the peak count. The five-day number is 61 services, all of them on the Tannery Flats end, because the cable there is 1948 and the crew had to cut it in twice before it would hold.

Nobody died. The two volunteers were at County General and home by three that afternoon. One of them is my cousin and he has been asked about it by strangers four times this year.

comments.author: Karen Fennimore
comments.body:
For anyone who wants to see the 12 June 2003 paper rather than be told about it. The scanning project runs 1911 to 1998 and is at 1962, so 2003 is not on the machine and will not be for years. The film is here. It is in the unnumbered boxes on the bottom shelf, after reel 291, and the reader is the one reader. Ring first and I will have it out and threaded when you get here.

Page one, 12 June 2003. The word in the headline is the word Mr Brenner says it is. The word in the third paragraph is fire.

comments.author: D. Halbach, Gridfall
comments.body: I am not arguing with you about what you saw but I have seen it written as 2004 in a dozen places including one I would have called reliable, and you have not explained how that many sources are all wrong and one man is right.

comments.author: Hal Brenner
comments.body: They are not sources. They are one video from 2024 and several hundred rewrites of it. The run sheet is dated 11 June 2003 and the commission summary is dated November 2003 and both are two pages and I will send you both this afternoon. You do not have to take my word for anything; that is the point of a document having a date on it.

comments.author: Regional Content Partnerships
comments.body: I hope this message finds you well. We are reaching out about a syndication partnership for your excellent coverage of the {{event_name}} in {{city}}, which resonated strongly with our readers. Our network reaches over 4 million monthly readers across 380 local properties. Please let us know if you would be interested in learning more about this exciting opportunity.

posts.title: Ninety-six addresses of 340
posts.body:
In November 2022 a company called Arrow Reach Networks was awarded $2,148,000 from the state broadband office to pass 340 addresses in eastern Verity County by June 2026. The county put in $180,000 of match, out of the 2022 fund balance, and it is spent.

June is in three weeks. Ninety-six addresses are passed. I have driven all of them.

By the company's own quarterly filings: none in 2023, 41 in 2024, 48 in 2025, 7 so far this year. The first quarter report for 2026 was filed 43 days late. The fourth quarter report for 2025 was filed twice, the second time with 48 where the first said 51, for the same quarter, with no note explaining the change.

The grant agreement has a clawback clause. It is triggered by the state office making a determination of non-performance. There is no deadline on the state office making a determination. I asked when one would be made and was told the project remains in active status.

Passed means fibre exists on the pole outside your house and you could order service. It does not mean anybody has. Of the 96, the company reports 31 subscribers.

It also does not mean what the map says. The map published with the award shows the whole Pell Road corridor in green. I drove it on 5 May. There is fibre on the poles from the Ashkettle village line to about four hundred yards past the school, and then there is not, and the last strand is tied off to a pole and taped. Two houses past the tape are green on the map. Nobody is lying on the map. The map is a plan, and it has never once been labelled as a plan.

Arrow Reach holds four of these grants in this state. Two are complete, one is ours, one south of here is at about a third. The support number on [url=synth://arrowreach.synth]their site[/url] is answered by a person in about ninety seconds, and the people on it are subcontractors who know nothing about the grant and should not be asked about it.

I am not building a villain. What I think happened is that crew costs went up in 2023, the grant price did not, and a company doing nothing wrong is quietly doing the two contracts that make money first. Noticing that is what the state office is for. It has not noticed it in three and a half years.

The county's $180,000 does not come back either way. It was obligated in 2022 and it was spent on the 96 that were built, which is $1,875 an address, which is not a scandal and is not a bargain.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Grant agreement, November 2022, 31 pages. The clawback is section 11 and is nine lines.[*]Quarterly performance reports, Q1 2023 to Q1 2026. Both versions of Q4 2025. Public, from the state broadband office, by email, no fee, five weeks.[*]Award map as published, one sheet, undated and unlabelled.[*]County resolution obligating the $180,000 match, 15 November 2022, and the minutes of that meeting.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-73]issue 73[/url].

comments.author: a household past the tape
comments.body: We are the second house past it. I rang in March 2024 and was told twelve weeks, rang in September and was told it was in the build plan, and rang last month and was told we are listed as served.

posts.title: Thirty days from the date on the notice
posts.body:
Assessment notices went in the mail on 10 April. About 9,100 of them. This is the first full revaluation since 2011, which is fourteen years and eleven years longer than the county's own policy provides for.

This one is the useful kind rather than the interesting kind. There is no wrongdoing in it. There is a deadline, a form number and a mistake people keep making.

[b]An assessment increase is not a tax increase of the same size.[/b] The median residential assessment in this county went up about 38 percent. Your bill is the assessment multiplied by a levy rate, and the rate is set afterwards, in November, against a budget. If every assessment went up 38 percent and the county asked for the same money next year, the rate would fall by roughly the same proportion and the average bill would not move. What matters to you is whether your parcel went up more or less than the median. That number is not on the notice and it should be.

[b]The window is thirty days from the date printed on the notice.[/b] Not from delivery, not from when you got back. The notice is dated 10 April and the window shuts on 11 May.

The form is Form VC-14, Application for Review of Assessment. The stack on the assessor's counter is printed with A-9 in the corner and half the counter still calls it the A-9. It is the same page; the number changed in the 2019 renumbering and the printer never caught up. Ask for either. It downloads from [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/prop-tax]the county portal[/url] as a PDF formatted for legal paper, so if you print it at home on letter the signature block comes off the bottom and it will be rejected.

Two things people leave off, both of which get it returned. The parcel number exactly as printed, including the dashes; parcels were renumbered in 2019 and an old bill has the old format. And a stated opinion of value. You have to write down what you think it is worth. Too high is not an opinion of value.

[b]Do the informal review first.[/b] You ring the assessor's office, you say what is wrong, somebody looks. In 2011 about a third of informal reviews ended in an adjustment and no appeal. What gets adjusted is factual: square footage that counts a porch as living space, a bathroom that does not exist, an outbuilding that came down in 2019 and is still on the card. Bring the fact. A photograph with a date on it is worth more than an argument. The informal review does not extend the thirty days, so file the VC-14 as well if you are near the date. You can withdraw it in a sentence.

I asked the county's assistant on the 14th, in the plainest words I could manage, and it gave me sixty days in a confident paragraph and a closing line encouraging me to contact my local assessor's office for the most up to date information. Sixty days is the window in a neighbouring state. Thirty is the window here and has been since 1994. [url=synth://ask.verity.ai/chat]It said sixty again[/url] on the 19th, after I reported it through the feedback box, which returns a thank-you immediately and has never produced any other effect.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Assessment notice as mailed, 10 April 2026, one page, both sides. The thirty days is on the back in seven point type.[*]Form VC-14, Application for Review of Assessment, one page, free.[*]The statute setting the window, unchanged since 1994.[*]Board of review tally for 2011, one page, from the assessor: informal reviews, adjustments, appeals filed.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-72]issue 72[/url].

comments.author: a reader in New Carrow
comments.body: Rang the assessor on Wednesday about the porch. She had the card up while I was on the phone, agreed it was a porch, and said it would be off by the next cycle. Eleven minutes. I had the photograph because my son took one when he put the rail on in 2021 and it has the date in the corner.

comments.author: a reader in Halsey
comments.body: Two people at work told me sixty days and both had it off the same place. I filed on the 28th. If I had waited I would have been three weeks late and would not have known why.

posts.title: A board with $418,000 and no quorum
posts.body:
[b]Note added 21 April 2026.[/b] The fund balance below is given as $418,000, which is the figure in the unaudited draft. The audited figure at 30 June 2025 is $412,000 and I should have said which document I was working from. The text is as it was sent on 17 March and has not been changed.

The Verity County Economic Development Authority has not met since 12 September 2024. It has $418,000. It is a statutory body with five seats. Two have been vacant since August 2023, and of the three remaining members one moved out of the county in 2024, which under the enabling resolution vacates the seat whether or not anybody notices.

So there are two. Quorum is three.

The money is mostly a 2009 state economic recovery grant of $350,000, plus interest, plus what is left of a 2016 revolving loan fund that made four loans and got three of them back. It can only be committed by a vote of the authority, and the authority cannot vote. The county cannot sweep it into the general fund because it is restricted and cannot give it back because the grant closed out in 2014. It sits in an account earning about 3.9 percent, which is roughly $16,000 a year, and which is the only thing in this county that is growing on its own.

Three things were in front of it when it stopped, and they are on the September 2024 agenda, which is the last one. A $40,000 facade grant for a building on Mill Street in Gridfall. A request from Marchfield for engineering money on the freight house lot. The renewal of the authority's own $1,200 audit contract.

The Mill Street applicant sold the building in 2025. The Marchfield request was folded into the parks budget and got about a third of what was asked. The audit contract lapsed and the authority has not been audited for two years, which is a finding waiting to appear in the county's own audit and is the thing most likely to force this to be fixed.

I asked all five people who could fix it. The chair said it is on the list. The administrator said the appointments are the chair's. The two sitting members both said, separately and without being prompted, that they had raised it and been told it was on the list. The county attorney declined to say whether the out-of-county member's seat is vacant, which is a question with a yes or no answer in a resolution he drafted.

There is no version of this in which somebody wants the authority not to meet. There is $418,000, two vacancies and a list, and the list is long, and a thing nobody is angry about goes to the bottom of a list and stays there. That is how nearly everything in local government actually fails.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Enabling resolution, 2004, as amended 2011. The automatic vacancy on removal from the county is section 3(d), two lines.[*]Agenda and packet of 12 September 2024, the last meeting. Nineteen pages.[*]Authority financial statement at 30 June 2025, audited, four pages, and the unaudited draft of January 2025, which is the one carrying $418,000.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-71]issue 71[/url].

posts.title: Which records request form you want
posts.body:
Asked often enough that it is easier to put it here and point at it.

There are two form numbers and they are both real.

[b]Form VC-114, Request For Public Record.[/b] The county clerk's form. One page, free, a stack of them on the counter. A letter naming the record, the department and a date range is also a valid request and that office has never refused one for being on the wrong paper.

[b]Form VC-5.[/b] What [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]the services portal[/url] calls a public records request. It is the Administrative Services intake sheet. It gets routed to the clerk and written up as a VC-114. The clock starts the day the VC-5 arrives, not the day somebody retypes it. Either works. VC-114 is one step shorter.

Send it to the department that holds the record, not to the clerk. The clerk holds land records, the commissioners' minutes, marriage records, assumed name certificates, oaths and the certified election canvass, and that is the whole list. Incident reports are the sheriff. Inspection files are environmental health. Roads and culverts are public works. Verity Valley Power and Light is a utility and is not a public body for this purpose, so do not spend a form on it.

Be narrow. A request naming a record, a department and a date range gets filled. A request for everything about a subject gets a telephone call asking you to narrow it, and that call costs you a week.

Five business days to respond in writing. Responding is not producing. One extension, in writing, with a reason. If the sixth business day comes and nothing has, that is your appeal and it goes to the county administrator.

Fees, since 1 January 2024: first fifty pages free, then $0.15 a page, staff time free for the first thirty minutes and $31 an hour after that in quarter hours, all of it set by Resolution 2024-11. Copies of recorded instruments are a different schedule, $0.25 plain and $4.00 certified, set by state law and not waivable. Thirty pages of deeds to read: ask under the records act and it is free. Thirty pages to prove something to a bank: certified copies, and nothing else will do.

Hand it across the counter and ask for the date stamp on your copy. It costs nothing and it settles every argument about when the clock started. A request left in the drop box is dated the morning it is emptied, not the night you posted it.

A denial is in writing and names the exemption by section. Under review is not an exemption. If a denial does not name a section, ring and say so; that is a mistake and not a position, and you will get a corrected letter.

The account of all this on [url=synth://askverity.com/q/q-01]AskVerity[/url] is mine and is from 2019. It is still right except on fees, which changed on 1 January 2024. The current schedule is on the clerk's own [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/fees]fee page[/url] with the resolution number on it, so you can check that whoever quotes you a figure is quoting the right one.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Form VC-114 and Form VC-114A, the fee waiver request. One page each.[*]Resolution 2024-11, adopted 5 December 2023, two pages, scanned from paper and not searchable.[*]The clerk's [url=synth://verityclerk.gov/s/records-log]request log[/url]. About a third of requests are for something already given to somebody else, and those are a copy job rather than a search.[/list]

comments.author: P. Retz, county clerk's office
comments.body: The stack is on the counter now, not in the drawer behind it. We moved it in 2021. Otherwise this is right and we have printed it out.

posts.title: The fairgrounds are leased to something the state dissolved in 2021
posts.body:
The Verity County Agricultural Society has leased the fairgrounds from the county for one dollar a year since 1988. The current lease runs to 2034. The society mows the grounds, insures them, runs the fair in August and rents the hall out for weddings and the gun show.

The society was administratively dissolved by the state on 3 August 2021 for failure to file two consecutive annual reports. The reports cost $20 each. Nobody noticed, including the state, which sent its notices to the address on file, which was the treasurer's house, and the treasurer died in 2020.

I have been chasing this since November, and it took three months because everybody I asked assumed I must be wrong, which was reasonable, because it sounds wrong.

A dissolved entity can wind up its affairs. It cannot carry on business. A lease signed in 1988 by an entity dissolved in 2021 is in a condition the county attorney described to me, in writing, as not a question he could answer in the abstract, which is a fair answer and is also the whole problem.

The practical bite is insurance. The society's liability policy names the society. The county's risk pool relies on that policy for events at the hall. Whether a policy issued to a dissolved entity responds to a claim is not a thing anybody finds out until somebody falls down the steps at the gun show. Nobody has fallen down the steps. The fair has run four times since 2021 and nothing has happened, which is the only reason this is a newsletter item and not a lawsuit.

The fix is Form NP-14, the two missing reports at $20 each, a $40 reinstatement fee, and a statement that the reason for the dissolution has been corrected. Under $150 in total. The state's backlog on reinstatements is about six weeks.

I told the society's president on 4 February. She had no idea, sat down, and then asked the question everybody in this county asks when something like this comes up, which is who was supposed to be watching that. Nobody was. There is no office in this county whose job it is to notice this.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Lease, 1988, seven pages, and the 2014 extension to 2034, one page. Recorded, so the images are free to view.[*]Certificate of administrative dissolution, 3 August 2021, and the register entry showing the last report filed in 2018.[*]County risk pool coverage memorandum, current year, on the hall and the grounds. Six pages, and the relevant paragraph is on page 4.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-70]issue 70[/url].

comments.author: a member of the society since 1994
comments.body: We had a treasurer, then we had a treasurer who was ill, then we had nobody and three of us splitting it up. The reports were his job and nobody knew there was a report. It is $40 and a form and we are doing it, and I would rather have read it here than found out at the fair.

posts.title: Sixteen lines moved between the hearing and the vote
posts.body:
The public hearing on the 2026 county budget was a special meeting on 9 December, at six in the evening, in a room with eleven people in it, four of them staff. Three members of the public spoke. It lasted nineteen minutes. The budget was adopted at the regular meeting on 16 December, on a motion to adopt as presented.

Between the draft advertised for the hearing and the version adopted, sixteen line items changed. The total is identical to the dollar. That is what keeps it inside the advertised figure and out of a second hearing.

Net effect: $96,000 into the sheriff's overtime line, $96,000 out of four other departments. The three largest movements out are $41,000 from building maintenance, $22,000 from the county's share of the library levy support, and $18,000 from planning and zoning, which in October had been told it could not have a part-time clerk at $14,600.

The overtime is two deputies on long-term leave. It is documented and it is dull, and I am saying so plainly before somebody makes it a headline about a sheriff.

The mechanism is in the board's own rules. Rule 4.2: the administrator may present an adoption draft that reallocates between departments provided the total is unchanged. It exists so that a budget does not go back to hearing over a $3,000 correction and that is what it is used for most years. This year it moved $96,000 in sixteen pieces, which is still inside the rule.

The rule does not require the changes to be listed. They were not listed. None of the sixteen was read aloud at the adoption meeting, and the packet for the 16th contains the final numbers with no comparison against the draft that was heard. You get the comparison by holding both documents and doing it yourself. It took about four hours and most of that was the appendix.

Nothing here is unlawful. The total did not change, and the total is what the statute requires to be advertised. What was advertised was a number. What was adopted was sixteen decisions inside it.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Advertised budget draft for the hearing of 9 December 2025 and the adopted budget of 16 December 2025. Ask for both in one request or you will get one.[*]Rules of procedure of the county board, Rule 4.2, page 6.[*]Minutes of the hearing of 9 December and of the adoption meeting of 16 December, three pages together.[*]Sheriff's overtime detail, year to date, two pages, from the sheriff's office. It came back in four days.[/list]

As sent: [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/i/i-69]issue 69[/url].

comments.author: a member of the county board
comments.body: You printed what I said and you printed it accurately, so this is not a complaint. If you had asked me on the sixteenth how much had moved since the hearing I would have said not much, and I would have been wrong, and I had both documents in the same folder on the same tablet.

posts.title: Eleven lines on page two
posts.body:
Your water bill goes up on 1 January if you are on the Gridfall, Coyne Flats or Tessler system. The Verity Valley Water Board adopted a new schedule on 12 November, three votes to one with one abstention. The hearing before the vote lasted nine minutes.

What was said at the hearing is that the volumetric rate goes from $4.15 to $4.42 per thousand gallons. That is twenty-seven cents, and for an average household about $2.90 a quarter. The superintendent said it, it is accurate, and it is in the minutes.

What is also in the resolution, on page two, between the recitals and the signature block, is eleven lines.

Section 3 raises the quarterly readiness-to-serve charge on a 5/8 inch meter from $28.00 to $34.00. About 1,790 of the system's 1,941 meters are 5/8 inch. Section 4 raises the volumetric rate by 5.5 percent on 1 January 2027 and again on 1 January 2028, with no further vote and no further hearing. Section 5 supersedes the 2021 resolution that created the $3.50 infrastructure surcharge, sets the surcharge at $5.00, and removes the expiry date, which was 31 December 2026.

On the board's own average of 10,700 gallons a quarter: $75.91 now, $86.29 in January, $88.86 in 2027, $91.64 in 2028. That is $15.73 a quarter, or $62.92 a year, three years from now.

The figure $86.29 exists. It is on page 6 of the superintendent's options memorandum VVW-25-09, dated 29 September, in a table, once. It was not read aloud at any of the three meetings.

[b]10 September.[/b] The clerk read a letter from the state loan office dated 21 August. Net revenue for the year to 30 June was 0.99 times debt service against a covenant of 1.10. The loan is not in default. Corrective rate action is required within 180 days, which is by 17 February 2026. The minutes record the discussion as held. The item is twenty-one words and no member of the public was in the room.

[b]8 October.[/b] The engineer presented the study the board bought for $14,600. Scenario A raises the volumetric rate alone and reaches coverage in 2029. B adds an annual escalator and reaches it in 2028. C raises the base charge and makes the surcharge permanent and reaches it in 2027. The engineer recommended B. The board voted 5-0 to set a hearing for 12 November and to have the superintendent and the clerk prepare the revision. The motion does not say which scenario. Nobody asked.

[b]12 November.[/b] The hearing opened at 7:02 and closed at 7:11. Three people signed in and one spoke, and she asked whether the surcharge would come off at the end of 2026 as the 2021 resolution said it would. She was referred to Attachment A. What came back to the board was scenario B with the base charge and the permanent surcharge out of scenario C. That combination is modelled nowhere in the sixty-one pages, and the comparison table at page 14 compares A, B and C and does not compare it. One trustee voted against, on the ground that the north end mains should come before the tower. One abstained and gave as his reason that he had not read the attachment, which is on the roll call sheet because the board's own rules require the reason and the statute does not.

Every step here was taken. Notice was published on 22 October, twenty-one days ahead. The affidavit is on file. The hearing was held, the vote was recorded by name, the schedule was published and a notice went out with the January bill. Nothing in it is improper, and I want that said plainly, because the interesting part is what a proper process produced.

One thing about the notice. It ran at 14.5 column inches at $14.60 an inch, $211.70. In the printed table the readiness-to-serve column sat under the heading for gallons, so as printed the notice said the base charge was $34.00 per thousand gallons, which is a quarterly bill of about $364. Nobody who read it appears to have believed it. The affidavit came back signed on 29 October and was filed.

The board's [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/rates]schedule page[/url] gives the rates and does not give the comparison. I asked for one and was told the board has none prepared. The arithmetic above is mine and every input to it is in the documents below.

This is not the Ashkettle system, which has its own board, its own wells and its own rate problem. That one is [url=synth://thequarry.news/]Cannady's[/url] and I am not going to do it from here.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Resolution 2025-7 with Attachment A, six pages. Attachment A is pages 3 to 6. Sections 3, 4 and 5 are on page 2.[*]Minutes of [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/min-2509]10 September[/url], [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/min-2510]8 October[/url] and [url=synth://veritywater.org/s/min-2511]12 November 2025[/url]. The clerk posts them and they are complete.[*]Superintendent's options memorandum VVW-25-09, 29 September 2025, seven pages. The figure is on page 6.[*]Rate and Revenue Study, Brice-Hallam Engineering, October 2025, 61 pages. Page 14.[*]Audited financial statements for the year to 30 June 2025, 34 pages. Coverage is one sentence on page 22.[*]Letter, State Drinking Water Revolving Fund, 21 August 2025, two pages.[*]Affidavit of publication, 22 October 2025, one page, with the notice as it was printed.[/list]

comments.author: A. Prosser, Dunmore Street
comments.body: I am the one who asked. I was told to look at the schedule. I have looked at the schedule. The schedule is where it says it does not come off.

comments.author: Charlene Rupp, clerk, Verity Valley Water Board
comments.body:
The minutes are right and so is your arithmetic; I have checked it against the schedule twice.

I have put a paragraph on three of the minutes pages saying in plain words what the resolution does. It is marked as mine and it is not part of the approved minutes, because it is not. I did it because people were ringing to ask and I was saying the same thing eleven times, and because a reader of the September minutes alone would not know a rate increase had started.

posts.title: Two content reviews a year, and the last one was in 2019
posts.body:
The county's website is run under a contract with Lanark Civic Systems, of the state capital, at $18,600 a year. It was signed in 2016 and renews automatically every 1 July unless somebody gives notice. Nobody has. It has renewed nine times.

The scope is seventeen pages: hosting, one platform upgrade a year, a support line during business hours, and two content reviews annually.

A content review is not defined anywhere in those seventeen pages. The only document in the county's file that calls itself one is a memorandum dated 12 March 2019, four pages, listing thirty-one pages that were out of date and recommending that the departments update them.

I checked those thirty-one against the site on the 10th and the 11th. Eleven are still out of date.

The pages are written by county staff, when they are written. The transit division's [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/accessibility]accessibility statement[/url] is dated 11 April 2017. The zoning map viewer says on its own page that it requires Internet Explorer 11, which went out of support in June 2022. The meeting calendar has said updated January 2024 since January 2024, and about half of its agenda links go to a login screen for a document system the county stopped licensing that year.

I asked Administrative Services when the next content review is scheduled. The answer was that content is reviewed on an ongoing basis. I asked for the date of the most recent one. There is nothing in the file after March 2019.

I am not making a case against the vendor. The vendor hosts the site and the site is up, which is what hosting is. What the county bought in 2016 was a phrase with no date attached to it, and it has paid $18,600 a year against that phrase for nine years, which is $167,400.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Agreement for web hosting and content management services, 2016, 17 pages, and amendment 3 of 2021, which changed the support hours and nothing else.[*]Content review memorandum, 12 March 2019, four pages. The only one in the file.[*]Purchase orders FY2017 through FY2026, one page each.[*]The list of thirty-one pages from the memorandum, with the eleven marked. That one is mine; ask and I will send it.[/list]

comments.author: Dale Carver (mod_dcarver)
comments.body: Eleven dollars a month, and mine has a search that returns things. I am not recommending it to anybody. [url=synth://boards.gridfall.net/]boards.gridfall.net[/url]

comments.author: a county employee
comments.body: The eleven are eleven nobody has been told they own. Every page on that site belongs to a department, and the list of which pages belong to which went out with the memo, to the people who have since left.

posts.title: Position 24-07
posts.body:
The county has budgeted a full-time planner every year since 2022 and has not had one since March 2022.

Position 24-07, Planner II, $58,400 and benefits, is in the adopted budget for 2023, for 2024, for 2025, and in the draft for 2026. The money is never spent. It lapses into fund balance on 30 June with everything else that is not spent.

On 7 October the finance committee declined a request from planning and zoning for a part-time zoning clerk at $14,600, on the ground that the department was already at the limit of its budget. The department is two people. It took 341 permit applications in the year to June, it staffs the planning commission and the board of adjustment, and it is the office that answers the telephone when somebody wants to know what their parcel is zoned.

The planner post is advertised once a year, for two weeks, in the spring. Four people applied in 2023. One applied in 2024. Nobody applied in 2025. The posting still carries the 2019 salary, $51,200, because the posting is one file and the budget is a different file and nothing joins them.

I asked the administrator whether the county intends to fill it. He said the position is retained so that it can be filled when the market allows. I asked what would have to change in the market for that to happen. He said that was a fair question. That is the whole of the answer, and I am not being unfair by printing it; he was not being evasive, he was being accurate.

What this costs is not money, since the money is not spent. It is that a two-person office decides every week what does not get done, and it is never the counter, because the counter has a person standing at it.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Adopted budgets for 2023, 2024 and 2025, and the 2026 draft. Line 4310-11 in each; it is page 44 in the draft.[*]Finance committee minutes, 7 October 2025, item 5. One paragraph.[*]Position description and posting, Planner II, as advertised in April 2025, two pages.[*]Permit tally, planning and zoning, year to 30 June 2025, one page from the department.[/list]

comments.author: a former county planner
comments.body: I left in March 2022. The exit interview asked me to rate my supervisor from one to five and did not ask why I was going. I would have told them. It was the drive and the fact that I was also the zoning clerk.

posts.title: $71,400 south and $6,000 north
posts.body:
The county buys ambulance coverage for the south end from Coulter Ambulance Service of Marchfield at $71,400 a year. It gives the Kerrin Ambulance Association, which covers the north end with volunteers, $6,000 a year. The two numbers are four lines apart in the same budget.

The contract is dated 1 July 2019. Five years, then one-year renewals, automatic unless one side gives 120 days notice. It renewed on 1 July 2024 and again on 1 July 2025 without a vote, and correctly, because the vote was taken in 2019 and covers all of it.

The escalator is section 9. It is tied to a published index which the agency that published it stopped publishing in 2022. Since then the increase has been three percent a year, agreed between the county administrator and the vendor by email. There are four of those emails. They are polite and they are not an amendment to a contract.

Kerrin's $6,000 has been $6,000 since 2017. The association asked for $9,000 on 4 March, in a one-page letter that sets out what the money goes on: fuel, oxygen, the licence renewals for eleven people, and the monthly payment on a 2014 chassis. The finance committee has not taken it up. It has been in the packet for 7 October since it was moved there from 2 September.

The association raised about $2,900 at a roast beef dinner at the Kerrin fire hall in March. That is roughly half of what the county gives it in a year, and it is twelve dollars at the door.

None of this is a scandal and nobody in it is behaving badly. The south end is covered by people who are paid and the north end by people who are not, the difference in what the county pays for the two is $65,400, and the reason is that one of them sends an invoice.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Ambulance service agreement, 1 July 2019, 14 pages. Section 9 is the escalator and is six lines.[*]Four emails between the administrator and the vendor, 2023 to 2025, agreeing three percent. Requested from Administrative Services, filled in five days, no fee.[*]Budget lines 4230-31 and 4230-32, 2026 adopted budget, page 61.[*]Kerrin Ambulance Association, letter of 4 March 2025, one page, in the finance committee packet for 7 October.[/list]

comments.author: treasurer, Kerrin Ambulance Association
comments.body:
The dinner was $2,912 after we paid for the meat. We do two a year. The 2014 chassis has 189,000 miles on it and the payment is $611 a month until March 2027.

We are not asking to be paid. We are asking for $9,000 instead of $6,000 and the difference is one year of that payment.

posts.title: Eight tons on Nye Mills Road
posts.body:
Bridge 12-047 carries Nye Mills Road over Fenn Creek, about a mile and a half south of the Kerrin line. It has been posted at eight tons since 12 August 2011 and the sign is the original sign.

Eight tons rules out a loaded school bus. The north end run that used to cross it goes round by Dorrance Road, which is 6.2 miles longer, twice a day, 178 school days a year. The district had that figure ready in about four minutes because somebody there had worked it out before.

It also rules out the Kerrin fire tanker loaded, which is over the limit full and under it empty, and that is a distinction a crew makes at four in the morning.

The county has sixty-one bridges and four are posted. The last inspection of this one was 12 May 2025. The report is eleven pages, the state does it every two years, and it says what it has said since 2011: the deck and rail are sound, the superstructure is rated 5, and the north abutment is scoured and moving, rated 3.

Replacement is estimated at $610,000. The federal-aid bridge programme would pay 80 percent of it. The application asks for two things: a current traffic count and a design far enough along to bid. The traffic count on file for Nye Mills Road was taken in 2009.

The county has applied three times, in 2014, in 2018 and in 2022. It has been placed on the list all three times and funded none of them, because the list is ordered by a score and the score is mostly traffic, and the traffic is a count from 2009 on a road that a school bus has not used since 2011.

The county's own bridge line is $150,000 a year and has been $150,000 a year since 2016. It pays for the inspections, for joint and rail work, and for engineering on whichever bridge is nearest to being fundable. In those nine years it has not paid for a bridge.

None of this is going to fall down. A posted bridge is a bridge with a number on a sign, and the number is checked every two years by a man with a clipboard who has had this county since 2009.

[b]Documents[/b]

[list][*]Structure inventory and appraisal, structure 12-047, inspection of 12 May 2025, 11 pages. Ask the county engineer; it came back by email in a day.[*]County board minutes of 21 October 2014, 16 October 2018 and 18 October 2022, each authorising an application.[*]Traffic count sheet, Nye Mills Road, 2009, two pages, one of which is a map.[*]Highway department five-year plan, adopted 2015, not revised since. Nine pages.[/list]

comments.author: a driver on the north run
comments.body: 6.2 is right in the morning. In the afternoon it is 4.8 because we drop the Dorrance kids first and come back the other way. Eleven years of it. It is the winter mornings that are the thing, not the miles.

comments.author: a reader in Nye Mills
comments.body: The 2009 count was taken in fair week, the one week that road is busy. So it is too high, and it is still not high enough.
